Get & Give Help

How you can get help and how you can help others.

Jump to:

Get Help

Need help because Hurricane Lowell affected your job, income, housing, food, utilities, or business? The resources below can help Kauaʻi residents, businesses, and non-profits navigate immediate needs and recovery.

Please note that information can change. Disaster recovery programs, eligibility requirements, hours, and availability may change. Please contact the organization directly to confirm current information before applying or visiting.

Last updated: October 12, 2026

Not Sure Where to Start?

  • Aloha United Way/ 211 can help connect you with available Hurricane Lowell recovery resources, including disaster case management, housing, financial assistance, supplies, and other support.

    Phone: 211 (dial to be connected directly to Aloha United Way resources)
    People can call 211 between 7 a.m. and 10 p.m. for assistance.

    Website: http://www.auw211.org

  • The Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster (VOAD) coordinates voluntary organizations providing disaster response and recovery assistance. Submit an intake form to request storm recovery assistance such as clean up, muck-out, and supplies.

    Intake Form: tinyurl.com/KauaiVOAD
    Website: www.hawaiistatevoad.org/kauai-coad/

Food Assistance

  • In partnership with the County of Kaua‘i, the Hawai‘i Foodbank Kaua‘i serves as the island’s disaster feeding lead. Below are their weekly emergency food distribution sites.

    Food Distribution Schedule

    Tuesday, October 13

    Hope Collective
    4303 Rice Street, Lihue
    (Mobile Pantry Distribution)

    Kekaha Neighborhood Center
    8130 Elepaio Road, Kekaha
    4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.
    Please bring your reusable bags or totes.

    Friday, October 16

    Hale Līhuʻe
    4286 Rice Street, Līhuʻe
    4:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.
    Turn into the parking lot from the Convention Hall, then exit toward Rice Street (right turn only).

    To respect local traffic, please line up no earlier than 15 minutes before the start time.

    For the most updated food distribution locations, please visit their website.

    https://kauai.hawaiifoodbank.org/

  • The Kaua‘i Independent Foodbank has food programs for children, seniors, and families in need.

    Phone: 808-278-6122; Available Monday- Friday from 9am to 3pm

    Website: https://www.kauaifoodbank.org/

  • On Sept. 10, 2026, the USDA approved the Hawaii Department of Human Services (HDHS) request to issue mass replacements to impacted households. This waiver approval allows households to receive replacement of SNAP benefits, as stated in the approval, due to power outages as a result of Hurricane Lowell that began on Sept. 7, 2026. The waiver approval applies to the island of Kaua‘i.

    In-person support: DHS staff will be on site at the Koloa and Hanalei Hurricane Resource centers on Tuesday, 9/22, and Thursday, 9/24, to provide in-person support for SNAP benefits.

    Website: https://humanservices.hawaii.gov/bessd/snap/

Lost Income & Employment

  • In-Person Services Update: Unemployment assistance will not be available at the Kōloa Resource Center on Thursday, Sept. 24. In-person help returns next week:

    • Hanalei Resource Center: Monday, Sept. 28, and Tuesday, Sept. 29

    • Kōloa Resource Center: Wednesday, Sept. 30, and Thursday, Oct. 1

    If you've had trouble applying online, meet with DLIR staff in person.

    Disaster Unemployment Assistance may become available following a qualifying federal disaster declaration for employees and self-employed individuals whose work is lost or interrupted as a direct result of the disaster.

    Apply: labor.hawaii.gov/ui
    Phone: 808-466-3634
    Kauaʻi Office: 808-274-3043
    Website: https://labor.hawaii.gov/ui/assistance-programs/disaster-unemployment-assistance-dua/

  • If your household income has decreased, you may now qualify for assistance even if you did not qualify previously.

    In-person support: Staff from the Department of Human Services will be on site at the Koloa and Hanalei Hurricane Resource centers on Tuesday, 9/22, and Thursday, 9/24, to provide in-person support for SNAP benefits.

    Phone: 855-643-1643

    Apply and learn more: pais.dhs.hawaii.gov

  • Gather Federal Credit Union (GFCU) Emergency Member Relief

    Provide qualifying members with additional financial flexibility through emergency assistance loans, loan payment deferrals, and penalty-free share certificate withdrawals.

    Learn more: https://www.gatherfcu.org/emergency-member-relief-program

Housing and Rent

  • If you are facing eviction or a housing crisis, these organizations may be able to help:

    Legal Aid – Landlord-Tenant Hotline: 800-499-4302

  • Family Life Center, Kaua‘i

    While they do not have additional funding to support hurricane victims, anyone from the houseless community can call and be screened for rental assistance and relevant services.

    Phone: 808-212-0850

  • Kauai Economic Opportunity (KEO)– Electric Bill Assistance

    Assistance may be available to eligible households struggling with electricity costs.

    KEO provides a one-time utility payment of up to $700 directly to electric or gas companies to restore service or prevent termination for qualifying low-income households on Kauaʻi. They are also offering assistance of up to $300 in partnership with Catholic Charities and KEO.

    Phone: 808-245-4077, ext. 242

  • Hawaiian Council’s just announced its statewide Host Housing Support Program for households hosting family, friends, or neighbors displaced by recent storms, including Hurricane Lowell.

    • Support: $500 per displaced person per month, up to $2,000 per host household per month, as funding allows.

    • Eligibility: Hawaiʻi residents hosting people whose primary residence was in a confirmed disaster-impacted area and was destroyed or sustained significant structural damage requiring extensive repairs.

    • Open to all: Applicants do not need to be of Native Hawaiian descent.

    • Housing requirements: Guests must stay in permanent housing with safe sleeping space, bathroom access, and a kitchen or cooking area. Tents and temporary shelters are not eligible. The home must pass a Housing Quality Standard inspection.

    • Documents: Identification for the host household and displaced adults, a completed W-9 for the host’s head of household, and documentation of the displaced household’s pre-disaster address. Monthly eligibility assessments are required.

    Deadline: Applications close October 14.

    —> Apply Here

    Questions or application assistance: kakoomai@hawaiiancouncil.org

Financial Assistance

  • Catholic Charities Hawaiʻi has the Hawaii Relief Program provides eligible families with assistance on rent (up to $6,000), utilities, vehicle payments, and other expenses following an involuntary loss or reduction of income or a natural disaster.

    Phone: 808-521-4357, Press 1, then 1
    HOPE Line: 808-241-4673

    Visit their Website

  • The Hawai‘i Realtors’ Disaster Relief Assistance offers relief grants are available to Hawaiʻi homeowners and renters affected by Hurricane Lowell. Grants of up to $1,000 are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Applications are due by November 4, 2026.

    Apply and Learn More Here.

  • Child & Family Services (CFS)

    • Concrete Support Program: Non-recurring, short-term financial assistance for eligible families with children.

    • Person-In-Needs Fund for Kupuna: Offers one-time maximum support of $500 for eligible persons 70 years old or older. (Due June 30, 2027)

    • Person-In-Needs Fund for Keiki: Offers one-time maximum support of $500 for eligible persons 18 years old or younger. (Due June 30, 2027)

    Phone: (808) 935-2188

    Visit their website for more information here.

  • The Office of Hawaiian Affairs is offering immediate disaster assistance for Native Hawaiian beneficiaries.

    OHA Board Authorizes More Than $360,000 in Emergency Relief for Native Hawaiians Impacted by Hurricane Lowell - The Office of Hawaiian Affairs (OHA)

    Apply here:

    Kauaʻi and Niʻihau - OHA Hurricane Lowell Recovery - Household Needs Intake Form

Small Business Recovery

If your business lost revenue, had to close, lost inventory or equipment, or struggling with payroll, rent, or other expenses because of Hurricane Lowell, the following resources may help.

  • Chamber of Commerce Hawaii is partnering with the State of Hawaii Department Business, Economic Development, & Tourism (DBEDT) to distribute $2.25 million in grant funding made available by the State of Hawaii to support non-agriculture small businesses on Kauai that have been impacted by Hurricane Lowell.

    Impacted businesses can receive $5,000 or $10,000 for disaster recovery.

    Apply Here

  • The Hawaii Small Business Development Center advisors can help small businesses with:

    • Evaluating losses

    • Cash flow

    • Financing options

    • Recovery planning

    • Small Business Administration (SBA) applications, when available

    Kauaʻi Center Office: Open, but currently restricted to remote advising
    Learn more: hisbdc.org

  • Kauaʻi Chamber of Commerce

    The Chamber can provide local recovery information, business-impact information, assistance opportunities, and coordination as new programs become available.

    Learn more: kauaichamber.org

     

    Kauaʻi Economic Development Board (KEDB)

    KEDB is another local resource for businesses navigating economic disruption, recovery, and available assistance programs.

    Learn more: kedb.com

  • Offered through the U.S. Internal Revenue Service, find federal tax-relief information and guidance for documenting losses, reconstructing records and addressing tax issues following a disaster.

    Website: https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/disaster-assistance-and-emergency-relief-for-individuals-and-businesses

  • Kalukalu @ 1624, a project by Kauai Federal Credit Union, is an economic resilience center for Kaua‘i. Located at 4-1624 Kuhio Highway, they are offering power, internet, and workspace for businesses and community members needing a place to work during recovery.

    Address: 4-1624 Kuhio Highway

    Drop in Hours: Monday - Friday, 9 AM - 4PM.

    Website: https://kauaicreditunion.org/kalukaluat1624/

  • Keep records of lost income and your inability to work because of Hurricane Lowell. Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA) may become available following federal approval and may include some self-employed workers who do not qualify for regular unemployment. Document your business's impacts and expenses, including:

    • Business closures

    • Canceled reservations or orders

    • Lost revenue

    • Payroll losses or expenses

    • Inventory losses

    • Property damage

    • Repair costs

    • Photographs

    • Insurance claims

    • Receipts

Commercial Farm & Ranch Recovery

  • The USDA has approved the Emergency Conservation Program (ECP) to address damages from Hurricane Lowell that occurred September 6, 2026 through September 9, 2026. ECP provides cost-share and technical assistance to producers to restore farmland to pre-disaster conditions following a qualifying natural disaster. ECP signup is open now and ends on November 13, 2026.

    Document your damage and connect with Calvin Threat for support. Access the form here.

    Calvin Threat
    County Executive Director, Kauaʻi County Farm Service Agency

    • 4334 Rice Street, Suite 103 Lihue, Hawaii, 96766

    • p: (808) 975-9532

    → Access the form here.

  • Hawaii Agriculture Disaster Response Tool to report disaster impacts, view statewide data, and find recovery and relief programs for Hawaii agricultural producers.

    Website: https://report.agstewardshiphawaii.org/

  • Kauai farm and ranch damage reporting and mini grant intake.

    Website: www.Tinyurl.com/FarmReporting

    Website: https://gofarmhawaii.org/gofarm-hawaii-flood-loss-assessment-tool/

Non-Profit Organizations

  • Offers funding for nonprofit organizations leading disaster response, recovery, and resilience efforts across Hawaiʻi. Through a single application, organizations can be considered by multiple participating funders within the Hawaiʻi Resilience and Recovery Funder Collaborative, including Hawaiʻi Community Foundation.

    Website: https://portal.justfund.us/p/rfps/51a042b6-c494-48ff-8734-2f51e6dad31b

  • The U.S. Small Business Administration announced the availability of low-interest federal disaster loans for eligible private nonprofit organizations in Hawaii impacted by Hurricane Lowell occurring Sept. 6 – 9.

    Who Can Apply

    • Private nonprofits & faith-based organizations

    Loan Assistance Available

    • Physical Disaster Loans: Repair or replace disaster-damaged property, equipment, inventory, and assets. Deadline: December 7, 2026.

    • Economic Injury Disaster Loans: Working capital assistance for operational expenses caused by the disaster. Deadline: July 7, 2027

    • Mitigation Funding: SBA disaster loans can be increased up to 20% of the verified losses to make building upgrades.

    Key Loan Details

    • Up to $2 million in loan funding

    • Interest rate as low as 3.625% for private nonprofit organizations

    • Loan terms of up to 30 years

    • No interest or required payments during the first 12 months following disbursement

    APPLY ONLINE: sba.gov/disaster

    Applicants may call the SBA National Support Network Center with questions regarding their application at (866)SBA-HELP or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov.

    For people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, please dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.

Federal Disaster Declaration Approved for Public Assistance

The White House approved a Major Disaster Declaration for Hurricane Lowell on Wednesday, Oct. 7. The declaration, FEMA-4952-DR-HI, follows Gov. Josh Green’s Sept. 9 request and covers the incident period of Sept. 6 to 9. The declaration makes federal Public Assistance available to Kauaʻi and Maui counties. Public Assistance helps state and county governments and certain nonprofits cover the costs of debris removal, emergency protective measures, and repairs to roads, bridges, public buildings, and utilities. It does not provide direct assistance to individuals or households. Individual Assistance is not part of this declaration at this time.

FEMA Individual Assistance, Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA), and SBA disaster assistance have been requested for Kauaʻi but are not yet available pending federal approval.

Save documentation of your losses and expenses.

What to track and save:

  • Proof of lost wages or reduced hours

  • Employer closure or layoff notices

  • Rent and utility bills

  • Receipts for disaster-related expenses

  • Photos of damage

  • Insurance information

  • Other documentation showing losses or expenses related to Hurricane Lowell

Give Help

We know many people want to help, but not all assistance sites have the capacity to sort physical donations, and unneeded goods can end up going to waste. Financial contributions are generally the most effective way to support recovery.

Here are a few meaningful ways you can help:

Financial Donations

Financial donations to trusted non-profit partners are the most effective way to support relief efforts, as they allow organizations to quickly respond to specific and changing needs.

  • Kaua‘i United Way

  • Hawaiʻi Foodbank Kaua‘i

  • Kaua‘i Independent Foodbank

  • Hawai‘i Community Foundation

  • Malama Kaua‘i

  • American Red Cross of Hawaiʻi

  • The Salvation Army Hawaiian & Pacific Islands Division

  • Kaua‘i Community College Student Aid

  • Other trusted non-profit and community partners supporting relief efforts

Where to Volunteer

If you are interested in volunteering, consider reaching out to established service providers with strong community networks, such as:

  • Kaua‘i Disaster Recovery Volunteer Sign-Up: Managed by Malama Kaua‘i and Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster (VOAD)

  • Hawaiʻi Foodbank Kaua‘i

  • American Red Cross of Hawaiʻi

  • The Salvation Army Hawaiian & Pacific Islands Division

  • Aloha United Way

  • Kaua‘i Independent Foodbank

  • Team Rubicon

  • Other trusted non-profit and community partners supporting relief efforts
